title: Psychological Methodologies
purpose: Seed plural psychological research methods so Lantern can investigate behavior, cognition, emotion and psychological constructs using experiments, observation, psychometrics, self-report, longitudinal and clinical/case evidence while preserving construct, sampling and interpretive limitations.

concepts.definition: A theoretical concept such as working memory, anxiety or motivation inferred through patterns of behavior/report/measurement rather than directly identical to one instrument score.
Methods for designing/evaluating measurements of psychological attributes, including reliability, validity, scaling and measurement invariance.
Consistency/stability of measurement under specified conditions; necessary for many uses but not sufficient for validity.
Evidence that a measurement behaves as expected for the intended construct and interpretation.
Evidence that a measure has sufficiently comparable measurement properties across groups/times for intended comparisons.
Participant-provided reports of thoughts, feelings, experiences or behavior, informative but affected by memory, interpretation, response style and context.
Observed/task-recorded behavior used as evidence about psychological processes under an explicit interpretation.
Biological/physiological signal used as evidence relevant to psychological questions; not automatically identical to a psychological construct.
Controlled manipulation/measurement methods used to test psychological hypotheses.
Systematic observation of behavior in relatively natural contexts with coding/sampling procedures.
Intensive study of an individual/small case, useful for description, rare phenomena and hypothesis generation but limited for population generalization.
Repeated study of psychological variables over time to examine development/change and temporal relations.
Study of psychological processes across cultural contexts with attention to construct/measurement comparability.
Features of a study that influence participants because they infer expectations/purpose.
Researcher/participant expectations can influence behavior, measurement or interpretation.
Tendency for responses to be shaped by perceived social acceptability.
Systematic response tendencies unrelated to the target construct.
Overreliance on Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich and Democratic populations that may limit generalization.
A clinical classification framework used under specified criteria; classification is not a complete explanation of an individual.
A theoretical/methodological tradition whose claims must be evaluated individually and historically rather than inherited wholesale as truth.

guards.reason: A measure can consistently measure the wrong thing.
A score is an indicator under a measurement model, not the construct itself.
Self-report is testimony/evidence about experience, not unmediated access to mind.
Biological signals require validated interpretation and may be multiply determined.
Case evidence can establish/illuminate a case and generate hypotheses but not population prevalence/effects alone.
Population/cultural scope must be justified rather than assumed.
Observed group differences can reflect many causal/social/measurement structures and do not establish immutable essence.
Diagnostic classification is a bounded clinical framework, not total identity/explanation.
Historical influence is not evidence that all theoretical claims are correct.
Interpretive/theoretical claims require evidence and should retain their school/method provenance.
Performance depends on task validity, context, state, strategy and measurement error.
Association does not identify psychological mechanism or causal direction.

invariants: Psychological constructs are theoretical objects inferred from evidence, not identical to individual scores or biomarkers.
Reliability and validity are distinct; reliability alone cannot establish validity.
Measurement comparability across groups/times requires invariance or other justification.
Self-report, behavior, physiology and task performance are different evidence types with different limitations.
Multi-method convergence can strengthen inference when limitations are sufficiently independent.
Case studies are valuable for cases/rare phenomena/hypothesis generation but have bounded population generalization.
Sampling/cultural scope is explicit; no sample silently becomes humanity.
Group-level differences do not establish immutable individual or group essences.
Demand characteristics, expectancy and response biases are methodological risks to evaluate.
Diagnostic categories are tools/classifications, not complete identities or causal explanations.
Historical schools/frameworks retain provenance and are evaluated claim-by-claim rather than inherited as truth.
Psychological claims preserve uncertainty, scope and methodology.

provenance.authoring_basis: Experimental, psychometric, observational, clinical/case, developmental and cross-cultural psychological methodologies adapted to Lantern's construct-validity and evidence architecture.
